flow_ref: User story (not in any OCMS flow deck)
code_summary: ocmsadminprivateapi framework/workflows/repccs/notice_creation/core/{CreateNoticeServiceImpl,helpers/SpecialVehUtils,helpers/NoticeProcessingHelper} (vehicle_registration_type D/I/V/S/F classification + PS-FOR + MID handling), crud/ocmsizdb/OcmsVipVehicle, agencies/lta/download/helpers (Diplomat path to RD1), agencies/mha/download/helpers/MhaNricDownloadHelper (PS-RIP/RP2), datahiveuenfin/DataHiveUenFinService (FIN death status), application.properties (ocms.vehicle.*). ocmsadminapi workflows/notice_creation/core/helpers/SpecialVehUtils (hardcoded copy). ocmsadminui, ocmseserviceapi, ocmseserviceui, thirdpartyapi: no code for this story.
note: Story status is Demo paid (50% of 75%), demo_remark: MID OK, FOR OK, RIP NOT OK (no Vault), DIP OK, VIP NOT BUILT. That remark is a claim, not proof: the code does have RIP and VIP (see steps 4 and 6). Vehicle type classification does run at notice creation, but its conditions (DIP suffix, MID markers) are read from application.properties, not from a parameter table maintained by an officer and not from a FOMS feed as the story says; the word FOMS appears nowhere in the six repos, so FOMS = CAS cannot be confirmed from repo. The ocmsadminapi copy uses the same rules but hardcoded, so the two places can drift. The Diplomat path after LTA uses the diplomaticFlag from the LTA file, not the result of the vehicle number classification. Property values on the real server and the content of LTA/MHA/CAS files cannot verify from repo. The story says Stored Procedure; no stored procedure was found in the repos, the logic is Java.
recommendation: Claim partially. The DIP/MID/FOR identification logic runs in code, but the rule source (properties, not a parameter table/FOMS) and the DIP path through the LTA flag differ from the story text. Do not claim full Sesuai until URA accepts properties as a replacement for the parameter table.

steps.step: OCMS determines the vehicle registration type of each notice from the vehicle number when the notice is created
steps.detail: checkVehregistration runs in order: source type F, blank or N.A becomes X, isDip becomes D, isMid becomes I, isVip becomes V, LTA validation becomes S, the rest F (SpecialVehUtils.java:57-106). processSingleNotice calls it and stores the result in the dto (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:707,714); numbers containing MID or MINDEF are forced to I first (:701-703). The sourceProvidedType parameter is always null (:707), so a source-provided type F is never used. The ocmsadminapi copy (staff/CES create notice) uses the same rules but hardcoded (SpecialVehUtils.java:100-118 in ocmsadminapi; CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:1027-1032), so it can drift from the properties version.

steps.step: Diplomat (DIP) vehicles are recognised from the prefix and suffix of the vehicle number that were set in advance
steps.detail: The rule works: the number must start with prefix S and end with CC, CD, TC or TE (SpecialVehUtils.java:114-121). But the values are read from application.properties (ocms.vehicle.diplomat.prefix and suffixes, application.properties:119-120; no override in application-prod.properties), not from a parameter table maintained by an officer and not from a FOMS feed as the story text says; changing the list needs a redeploy. There is no list of DIP vehicle numbers, only a pattern. In ocmsadminapi the same pattern is a hardcoded regex (SpecialVehUtils.java:100-106). Property values on the real server cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: Military (MID) vehicles are recognised from a MID or MINDEF prefix or suffix on the vehicle number
steps.detail: isMid matches when the number starts or ends with one of the markers MID or MINDEF (SpecialVehUtils.java:128-131); the markers are read from ocms.vehicle.mid.markers (application.properties:122), and CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:701-703 even uses a looser contains MID or MINDEF before isMid is called. Same as the DIP step: the source is properties, not a parameter table or FOMS, so the fit is the same (Sebagian). In ocmsadminapi it is hardcoded (SpecialVehUtils.java:113-118 in ocmsadminapi).

steps.step: VIP vehicles are recognised from a list of vehicle numbers stored in a table
steps.detail: isVip looks the number up in table ocms_vip_vehicle and only counts status A (SpecialVehUtils.java:138-149; OcmsVipVehicleServiceImpl.java:79-90). The table is filled by the daily 02:00 CAS refresh cron (cron.casvipvehicle.enabled=true, cron-schedules-prod.properties:336-337) from CAS getVIPVehicles (application-prod.properties:112). The story says FOMS; FOMS = CAS cannot be confirmed from repo. If the query errors, isVip returns false (fail-open, SpecialVehUtils.java:144-147), so a VIP can pass as S. The TS-CLV assignment in Toppan does not use the table but a regex for numbers starting with V (ToppanUploadHelper.java:706). Ticket OCMS-SR-2026-051 (Closed): the table content was once patched through a DB script. The demo remark VIP NOT BUILT does not match the code: the VIP feature exists, only its source is not proven to be FOMS.

steps.step: Foreign vehicles (FOR) are recognised and the notice is given suspension FOR right away
steps.detail: A number that does not pass D, I, V and the LTA validation falls to type F (SpecialVehUtils.java:105-106). For type F, setForeignVehicleSettings fills PS-FOR in the dto (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:482-484), the notice is created, then createForeignVehicleSuspension saves a suspended_notice row with reason FOR (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:797-799,867-873; NoticeProcessingHelper.java:578-579). If the notice is a duplicate (DBB), PS-FOR is skipped (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:801-810). It is also used as the indicator for the 90-day admin fee (outside this story, see orphans).

steps.step: Notices of an ID whose life status is deceased are recognised and given suspension RIP
steps.detail: NRIC path: an MHA result with lifeStatus D and a Date of Death is used; a DoD on or after the offence date gives PS-RIP, before the offence gives PS-RP2 (MhaNricDownloadHelper.java:872-874,953-966,1017-1021). The MHA download cron is enabled=true (cron-schedules-prod.properties:119-120). A FIN path via DataHive also exists (DataHiveUenFinService.java:3310-3317) but its job is switched off in prod: cron.mhadownload.uenfin.enabled=false (cron-schedules-prod.properties:52; checked in MhaDownloadJobsScheduler.java:43,104). So only some IDs are covered. Demo remark RIP NOT OK, no Vault: the code does not use Vault, the sources are MHA/DataHive. Real MHA file content and server values cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: Military (MID) notices go straight to the reminder stage with the MINDEF owner and address filled in automatically
steps.detail: For type I, processMilitaryVehicle sets the last stage to NPA and the next stage to RD1 (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:609-615; called at CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:812-813), then populateAddressForMilitary creates the MINDEF owner row and mha_reg address from constants (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:727-765; SystemConstant.java:252-265; called at CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:912-914). The ID and address values are hardcoded in SystemConstant; whether they match the official MINDEF data cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: Diplomat (DIP) notices are moved to the reminder stage after they are identified
steps.detail: A D notice is created through the V/S/D path: last NPA, next ROV (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:438-441). After the LTA result, diplomaticFlag Y makes the record count as Diplomat and the stage is set to ROV then next RD1 (LtaDownloadHelper.java:418-425; LtaProcessingOrchestrator.java:101-109; LtaProcessingStageManager.java:511-552). The LTA download cron is enabled=true (cron-schedules-prod.properties:148-149). The gap: the Diplomat decision at the LTA stage uses the flag from the LTA file (LtaBatchCode0Processor.java:254-258), not the result of the S..CC number classification in the DIP step, so a D-by-prefix notice whose LTA flag is N goes through the standard path. Ticket OCMS-DF-2026-052 (Closed, Prod deployed): the Diplomat stage was once wrongly set to ENA instead of RD1 because of a cache bug; it has been fixed. Real LTA file content cannot verify from repo.
